title: Quote drafts from site photos and voice notes
description: Take photos on site, speak the measurements and notes into your phone. You get a quote draft in your own template to check and send.
gdpr: Photos and customer addresses. Use an EU-hosted tool or a business plan with no training on your data. Remove faces from photos.
readiness: You (the owner) learn it in 2 evenings. The office assistant learns to finish and send drafts in 1 hour.
tools: ChatGPT Team or Microsoft 365 Copilot with your Word template
notWorthItReason: You write fewer than 2 quotes a week. Your templates are faster than learning a new tool.

plan: Day 1–2: Load 10 of your past quotes and your price list into the tool as examples.
Day 3–7: For every new site visit, take photos and record a 2-minute voice note. Let the tool draft the quote.
Day 8–12: Check each draft, fix it, send it. Note how long each one took.
Day 13–14: Compare with your usual time per quote. Keep it, adjust it, or drop it.
pilot.metric: Time per quote drops from about 1 hour to 25 minutes, and no quotes written after 8 pm.

title: Text-block library in your trade software
description: Set up your 30 most common positions once (prep, primer, two coats, scaffolding). Quotes become click-and-adjust.
gdpr: No new data processing. Stays in your existing software.
readiness: One afternoon to set up. Everyone who writes quotes learns it in 30 minutes.
tools: Your current trade software (most have text blocks)

plan: Day 1: List the 30 positions you write most often.
Day 2–3: Enter them as text blocks with prices.
Day 4–14: Use them for every quote. Add missing ones as you go.
pilot.metric: Quote time down 30% within two weeks.

title: Automatic follow-up on open quotes
description: If a customer hasn't answered after 7 days, a friendly reminder goes out by email. You stop losing jobs to silence.
gdpr: Customer email addresses, already in your system. Use your own mail account, no new provider needed.
readiness: Office assistant sets it up in 1 hour.
notWorthItReason: With very few quotes, a note in your calendar does the same job for free.

plan: Week 1: Turn on reminders for every quote older than 7 days.
Week 2: Count replies to reminders.
pilot.metric: At least 1 extra accepted quote in 2 weeks.

title: AI phone answering and callback assistant
description: When you're on site and can't pick up, a friendly voice assistant takes the call, notes name, number and request, and sends it to your WhatsApp.
extraValueLabel: jobs no longer lost to missed calls
gdpr: Caller voice, name and number. Choose an EU-hosted provider with a data processing agreement (AVV). The assistant must say it is automated.
readiness: Set up in one afternoon. Crew leads learn to read the WhatsApp summaries; nobody else has to change anything.
notWorthItReason: You miss fewer than 1 call a day. A normal voicemail with text transcription is enough.

plan: Day 1: Forward calls you don't answer within 20 seconds to the assistant.
Day 2: Give it your opening hours, services and areas served.
Day 3–14: Read each call summary in WhatsApp and call back within 2 hours. Mark which calls became jobs.
pilot.metric: Zero unanswered calls, and every caller called back the same day.

title: Voicemail to text in your inbox
description: Your phone provider turns voicemails into text messages, so you can read them between jobs instead of listening.
gdpr: Voicemail content. Stays with your telephone provider.
readiness: 10 minutes to switch on. No training.

plan: Day 1: Turn on transcription.
Day 2–14: Read instead of listen.
pilot.metric: Callbacks within the same day.

title: Website FAQ assistant
description: A small chat on your website answers the usual questions (areas served, opening hours, how to get a quote) and takes callback requests.
gdpr: Visitor messages, name and phone. EU hosting, cookie-free widget, clear notice that it is automated.
readiness: Set up in 1 hour from your existing website text. Office checks requests once a day.
notWorthItReason: Your website gets around 20 visitors a month. A chatbot would answer almost nobody. Put your phone number and a callback form at the top instead.

plan: Day 1: Load your website text.
Day 2–14: Check every conversation it had and fix wrong answers.
pilot.metric: At least 5 callback requests captured outside office hours.

title: WhatsApp Business with quick replies and labels
description: Separate business and private chats, ready-made replies for the 10 usual questions, and labels for new / quoted / booked.
gdpr: WhatsApp is not ideal for customer data (US provider). Fine for crew chat; for customers get consent or move to an EU messenger later.
readiness: 30 minutes. Everyone on the phone learns it in a day.

plan: Day 1: Install and add 10 quick replies.
Day 2–14: Label every new request.
pilot.metric: No customer message unanswered for more than 24 hours.

title: Online booking for site visits
description: Customers pick a free slot for a viewing from your calendar. No more phone tag to find a date.
gdpr: Name, phone, address. Use an EU-hosted booking tool (e.g. Cal.com EU) or Microsoft Bookings in an EU tenant.
readiness: Set up in 1 hour. Office assistant keeps the calendar up to date.

plan: Day 1: Block 3 viewing slots a week.
Day 2–14: Send the booking link instead of calling back.
pilot.metric: Half of all viewings booked without a phone call.

title: Shared crew planning board
description: One board everyone sees on their phone: which crew, which site, which material. Replaces the 6:30 phone round.
gdpr: Employee names and job addresses. Choose a German provider with an AVV.
readiness: Crew leads need 1 hour of training. Expect 2–3 weeks before everyone checks the board instead of calling.
notWorthItReason: With under 5 people, a shared calendar does the job.

plan: Week 1: Plan one crew on the board only.
Week 2: Add all crews, stop the morning phone round.
pilot.metric: Morning briefing done in 15 minutes instead of 45.

title: Custom AI scheduling agent
description: A custom-built AI that plans crews, sites and material automatically.
gdpr: All employee and job data in a custom system. Needs its own data protection review.
readiness: Months of setup. Everyone has to change how they work.
notWorthItReason: Your existing calendar or a planning board does 80% of it for a fraction of the cost. Payback would take years.

title: Voice-note logging of extra work on site
description: When the customer asks for 'just one more wall', the crew lead says it into the phone. It becomes a billable item on the invoice, with photo and time.
extraValueLabel: extra work that now gets billed
gdpr: Voice notes and site photos. EU-hosted transcription, delete audio after 30 days.
readiness: Crew leads learn one habit: one voice note per extra job. Plan 2 weeks of reminders before it sticks.
notWorthItReason: You rarely do unplanned extra work, so there's little to recover.

plan: Day 1: Brief crew leads: one voice note per extra job, with a photo.
Day 2–14: Office turns notes into invoice items every Friday.
pilot.metric: Every extra job in the 2 weeks appears on an invoice.

title: Automatic payment reminders
description: Your accounting software sends polite reminders when an invoice is overdue. No awkward calls.
gdpr: Customer data already in your accounting software. No new provider.
readiness: Office assistant, 30 minutes.

plan: Day 1: Turn on reminder levels (7, 14, 21 days).
Day 2–14: Watch overdue invoices.
pilot.metric: Overdue amount down 30%.

title: Receipt capture for your tax advisor
description: Snap receipts with your phone. They go straight to your tax advisor, sorted.
gdpr: Receipts. DATEV and Lexware host in Germany.
readiness: Ask your tax advisor; most set it up for free.

plan: Week 1–2: Photograph every receipt the day you get it.
pilot.metric: No shoebox at month end.

title: AI-drafted email replies
description: Your mail program suggests replies to routine emails (dates, documents, quote questions). You check and send.
gdpr: Email content. Business plans of Microsoft and Google don't train on your data; keep it in an EU tenant.
readiness: 1 hour for the person who handles email.

plan: Week 1–2: Use drafts for every routine email; note the time saved.
pilot.metric: Email time down by 1 hour a week.

title: Site reports from photos
description: Daily site log (weather, crew, progress, problems) written from photos and a short voice note. Protects you in disputes.
gdpr: Site photos. Avoid faces, German or EU hosting.
readiness: Crew leads: 30 minutes. Habit takes 2 weeks.

plan: Week 1–2: One report per site per day.
pilot.metric: Reports for every site, every day.

title: Automatic Google review requests after each job
description: After the final invoice, the customer gets a short thank-you with a link to leave a review. More reviews, more calls.
gdpr: Customer email or phone, only with consent (ask at handover).
readiness: Office assistant, 30 minutes.
tools: Google Business Profile review link + email template

plan: Week 1–2: Send the review link with every final invoice.
pilot.metric: 5 new reviews in 2 weeks.

title: Before/after posts from site photos
description: AI writes short posts from your before/after photos for Instagram and Google.
gdpr: Customer property photos. Ask the customer first; no house numbers or faces.
readiness: Apprentice or office: 1 hour.
notWorthItReason: Your order book is already full. More visibility means more calls you can't answer.

plan: Week 1–2: One post per finished job.
pilot.metric: 4 posts, 1 enquiry.

title: Wall-painting robot
description: A robot that sprays walls and ceilings on large sites.
gdpr: No personal data. Safety assessment and site rules apply.
readiness: Operator training of several weeks; only pays on large, empty, repetitive surfaces.
tools: Rent from a robotics service provider
notWorthItReason: At 14 people, mostly occupied homes and small sites, the robot would stand still most of the year. Payback well over 10 years.

title: Order intake via WhatsApp and phone
description: Cake and catering orders come in by WhatsApp or the phone assistant and land in one order list with pickup date and shop.
gdpr: Customer name, phone, order. EU-hosted, AVV, automated notice.
readiness: Shop staff learn the order list in 30 minutes.

plan: Day 1: Connect WhatsApp and phone to one order list.
Day 2–14: Every pre-order goes through the list only.
pilot.metric: Zero lost or double orders in 2 weeks.

title: Daily production forecast
description: Uses your sales history, weekday, weather and holidays to suggest how much of each product to bake. Less left over.
gdpr: Sales data only, no personal data.
readiness: Head baker checks the suggestion every evening; trust grows over 4 weeks.

plan: Week 1: Track leftovers per product per shop.
Week 2: Bake to the forecast for 5 products.
pilot.metric: Leftovers down 20% on those 5 products.

title: Staff shift planning app
description: Shifts for both shops in one app. Staff swap shifts themselves; you approve with one tap.
gdpr: Employee data. German provider with AVV.
readiness: Staff install the app in 10 minutes.

plan: Week 1–2: Plan both shops in the app only.
pilot.metric: Shift plan done in 30 instead of 90 minutes.

title: Cobot arm for tray loading
description: A collaborative robot arm loads and unloads baking trays at night.
gdpr: No personal data. Machine safety assessment needed.
readiness: One person trained as operator (1 week). Bakehouse layout must change.
notWorthItReason: With 2 shops and changing product ranges, the arm would idle most of the night. Check again above roughly 2,000 trays a week.

title: Floor-cleaning robot
description: Cleans shop or workshop floors after closing.
gdpr: Robots with cameras: no recording, inform staff.
readiness: Staff learn to start it in 15 minutes.
notWorthItReason: Your floor area is small. A cleaner for 30 minutes costs less.

plan: Week 1–2: Rent one, run it every night.
pilot.metric: Cleaning time down 60%.

title: Cutting list optimisation
description: Software plans cuts from your sheet material so less wood ends up as waste.
gdpr: No personal data.
readiness: Workshop lead: 1 day.

plan: Week 1–2: Plan every sheet cut with the tool.
pilot.metric: Offcut waste down 15%.

title: Automatic palletizer
description: Stacks finished goods onto pallets at the end of a line.
gdpr: No personal data.
readiness: Two operators trained (1 week).
notWorthItReason: Only pays with steady volume over at least 2 shifts a day.
